presentation.name: Core symptoms
presentation.def: Cardinal features of the condition itself, in any system, including its characteristic pain

presentation.name: Time course
presentation.def: Onset, duration, pattern, progression, chronicity, diurnal or exacerbation pattern

presentation.name: Prodromal
presentation.def: Symptoms or warning signs before the main event (aura, prodrome)

presentation.name: Postdromal
presentation.def: Symptoms after the main event (postictal, post-attack recovery)

presentation.name: Systemic
presentation.def: Fever, sweats, weight change, fatigue, appetite, malaise; heat/cold intolerance, thirst, polyuria, hormonal symptoms

presentation.name: Cardiorespiratory
presentation.def: Chest pain, palpitations, oedema, syncope, claudication, perfusion and rhythm symptoms; breathlessness, cough, sputum, wheeze, haemoptysis, upper-airway symptoms

presentation.name: Abdominal and pelvic
presentation.def: Dysphagia, reflux, nausea, abdominal pain, bowel habit change, bleeding, jaundice; urinary, sexual, menstrual, fertility and obstetric symptoms

presentation.name: Neurological
presentation.def: Neurological symptoms of any kind: headache, seizures, cognition, vertigo, weakness, tremor, rigidity, gait, numbness, paraesthesia, autonomic symptoms, speech and swallowing

presentation.name: Musculoskeletal and skin
presentation.def: Joint, bone, muscle and back symptoms, stiffness, deformity; rash, ulcers, lumps, pruritus, mouth and mucosal symptoms

presentation.name: Special senses
presentation.def: Visual loss, red eye, visual disturbance; hearing loss, tinnitus, otalgia, vertigo of ear origin

presentation.name: Acute on chronic
presentation.def: Features of an acute exacerbation or decompensation on top of the chronic condition (heart failure exacerbation, uraemia in CKD, COPD exacerbation, DKA, adrenal crisis)

presentation.name: Complications
presentation.def: Complications of the disease or its treatment that the patient may report

presentation.name: Red flags
presentation.def: Alarm features that need urgent escalation

presentation.name: Impact
presentation.def: Functional, work, emotional, psychosocial and quality-of-life effects

risks.name: Non-modifiable and genetic
risks.def: Age, sex, ethnicity, pregnancy, hormonal, anatomical and congenital predispositions; family history and inherited conditions

risks.name: Lifestyle and exposures
risks.def: Smoking, alcohol, diet, obesity, inactivity, substance use, behaviours; occupational, environmental, travel, allergen and contact exposures; prior or concurrent infections

risks.name: Drugs and procedures
risks.def: Medicines that cause or predispose (iatrogenic, nephrotoxins, steroids); surgery, lines, devices, dialysis access, instrumentation

risks.name: Comorbidities
risks.def: Existing diseases that cause or predispose, including autoimmune, metabolic and past history

risks.name: Triggers
risks.def: Precipitants of onset, attack or decompensation

examination.name: General and vitals
examination.def: Appearance, observations, nutrition, hydration, general inspection; signs of severity or decompensation

examination.name: Cardiorespiratory
examination.def: Pulses, heart sounds, murmurs, BP, perfusion, vascular signs, oedema; chest inspection, percussion, auscultation, breathing pattern, sputum

examination.name: Abdomen
examination.def: Abdominal inspection, palpation, organomegaly, ascites, hernias, rectal

examination.name: Neurological
examination.def: Cranial nerves including vision, eye signs and hearing, tone, power, reflexes, sensation, coordination, gait, cognition

examination.name: Musculoskeletal and skin
examination.def: Joints, spine, muscles, deformity, range of motion; skin, nails, hair, rash, bruising, skin ulcers

examination.name: Local and peripheral signs
examination.def: Findings at a specific site (ulcer, lump, stoma, access site, wound, prostate, genitalia, mouth, ears, nose, throat, thyroid, lymph nodes) and signs outside the primary organ (stigmata, extra-articular, extra-intestinal, associated disease)

examination.name: Special tests
examination.def: Named signs and manoeuvres and bedside severity tests

examination.name: Complications
examination.def: Signs of complications, metastases, spread or end-organ damage

investigations.name: Bedside and functional
investigations.def: Point-of-care and clinic-based tests (obs, ECG, urinalysis, BSL, bedside spirometry, scores and questionnaires); physiological function tests (lung function, urodynamics, sleep studies, neurophysiology, audiometry, stress tests)

investigations.name: Bloods
investigations.def: Any blood test, including markers, serology, drug levels, glycaemic control and clotting

investigations.name: Urine, stool and microbiology
investigations.def: Urine and stool tests (ACR, 24h urine, FOBT/FIT, calprotectin, stool studies); cultures, swabs, PCR, tap fluid and other tests for infection

investigations.name: Imaging
investigations.def: X-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI, nuclear, echo, angiography, DEXA

investigations.name: Endoscopy and tissue
investigations.def: Scopes and direct visualisation (gastroscopy, colonoscopy, bronchoscopy, cystoscopy); biopsy, cytology, histology, molecular and genetic tests

investigations.name: Screening and monitoring
investigations.def: Screening programs, risk scores, pre-treatment checks, diagnostic criteria; staging work-up, ongoing disease monitoring and surveillance

medications.name: Acute and first line
medications.def: Emergency and acute-phase treatment (thrombolysis, resuscitation, exacerbation, rescue); initial standard drug therapy

medications.name: Escalation and disease-modifying
medications.def: Add-on, second-line, resistant-disease and advanced therapies; treatments that change disease course (DMARDs, immunotherapy, antivirals, anti-cancer, curative)

medications.name: Symptomatic and palliative
medications.def: Symptom relief and supportive drugs (analgesia, antiemetics, bronchodilator relievers); palliative and end-of-life care, advance planning

medications.name: Procedural
medications.def: Surgery, drainage, revascularisation, devices, transplantation, other interventions

medications.name: Non-drug
medications.def: Lifestyle, diet, rehab, physiotherapy, allied health, self-management, education

medications.name: Prevention and monitoring
medications.def: Primary and secondary prevention, prophylaxis, vaccination, risk-factor control; follow-up, drug monitoring, safety checks, surveillance

medications.name: Avoid
medications.def: Drugs, interventions and behaviours to avoid or use with caution because they are contraindicated, harmful or precipitate decompensation (e.g. nitrates in aortic stenosis, NSAIDs in heart failure and CKD)

differentials.name: Cardiorespiratory
differentials.def: Heart, rhythm, lung and airway causes that don't fit a mechanism category

differentials.name: Gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary
differentials.def: Oesophageal, gastric, bowel, anorectal, liver, biliary and pancreatic causes that don't fit a mechanism category

differentials.name: Renal, urological and reproductive
differentials.def: Kidney, bladder, prostate, genital, gynaecological, breast and obstetric causes that don't fit a mechanism category

differentials.name: Neurological and psychiatric
differentials.def: Central and peripheral nervous system, mental health and behavioural causes that don't fit a mechanism category

differentials.name: Musculoskeletal and skin
differentials.def: Bone, joint, muscle, soft-tissue and dermatological causes that don't fit a mechanism category

differentials.name: Eye, ear, nose and throat
differentials.def: Ocular and ENT causes that don't fit a mechanism category

differentials.name: Endocrine, metabolic and haematological
differentials.def: Endocrine, metabolic, nutritional, electrolyte, blood, coagulation and platelet causes

differentials.name: Infective and inflammatory
differentials.def: Infections and inflammatory or autoimmune causes of any organ, when clearly so

differentials.name: Malignant
differentials.def: Cancers and neoplasms of any organ, when clearly so

differentials.name: Vascular
differentials.def: Ischaemic, thrombotic, embolic and haemorrhagic vascular causes in any organ

differentials.name: Structural and traumatic
differentials.def: Mechanical, anatomical, obstructive, congenital and traumatic causes

differentials.name: Drugs and toxins
differentials.def: Medicines, alcohol, substances, poisons and withdrawal

differentials.name: Physiological and functional
differentials.def: Normal physiology, variants and functional disorders

associated.name: Characteristics and course
associated.def: Nature, severity, location, distribution and quality of the main symptom; onset, duration, progression, timing, pattern; triggers and aggravating or relieving factors

associated.name: Event and collateral
associated.def: Details of a discrete event and witness or collateral history

associated.name: Constitutional
associated.def: Fever, sweats, weight change, fatigue, appetite

associated.name: Abdominal and pelvic
associated.def: GI symptoms including bowel and rectal; urinary, sexual, gynaecological and breast symptoms

associated.name: Neurological and special senses
associated.def: Neurological symptoms; eye, ear, nose and throat symptoms

associated.name: Musculoskeletal and skin
associated.def: Joint, muscle, bone and skin symptoms

associated.name: Psychological and social
associated.def: Mood, anxiety, cognition, psychosis, sleep, psychiatric history; social circumstances, function, independence, impact on life

associated.name: Red flags
associated.def: Alarm features that need urgent escalation

associated.name: Past history
associated.def: Relevant past medical and surgical history, previous episodes, screening

associated.name: Drugs and substances
associated.def: Medications, alcohol, tobacco and recreational substances

associated.name: Risk factors and exposures
associated.def: Demographic, lifestyle and family risk factors; travel, occupational, environmental, infective contacts, allergens
